symptoms: High volume of open refund-related support tickets (backlog) prompting the chatbot request.

causal_chain: Refunds submitted for processing fail IBAN-format validation at the payment step (E-01: 5/5 refund_failures records show FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT).
Failed refunds remain unresolved for the customer, who is not notified of a definitive outcome.
Affected customers open or repeat support tickets to check status of the stuck/failed refund, inflating ticket volume.
This repeat-contact volume accumulates into the observed ticket backlog.

proposal.summary: The initial request (from SH-SUP, support lead) was to build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for refund-status answers, framed as a response-speed problem (CL-01/CL-02). Investigation evidence contradicted that framing: ticket-db showed agents responding in a median of 2.0 hours against a 24-hour SLA across 900 tickets (E-02), while payment-db showed all 5 sampled refund failures were FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01) — a technical refund-validation failure, not a response-time issue. The problem definition (PD-1) was therefore reframed around the IBAN-format failure as the likely backlog driver, rejecting hypothesis H-RESPONSE-SPEED and supporting H-RECURRING-PAYMENT-FAILURES. The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two critical/high unknowns about the actual failure-to-ticket correlation and competing causes as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than resolving them pre-release. Given this, the release scope was narrowed to a single achievable deliverable from DA-PAY: quantifying the IBAN-format failure count (5 failures, M-IBAN-FAILURE-COUNT). The system issued a RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION decision with no holds — the narrow, verified count was shipped, while the harder work (ticket-correlation join, root-cause fix, failure-rate denominator) was left open and explicitly logged as limitations. No chatbot or response-speed remedy was built, consistent with the success criterion that rejected that approach.
key_points: Initial request (CL-01/CL-02, stakeholder SH-SUP): build a chatbot because customers wait too long for refund status answers.

Evidence contradicts the speed framing: E-02 shows median agent response time of 2.0h against a 24h SLA across 900 tickets, and E-01 shows all 5 observed refund_failures records are FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, not slow replies.

The root problem was redefined (PD-1) as a recurring IBAN-format refund-validation failure (E-01) generating repeat tickets, not slow support; hypothesis H-RESPONSE-SPEED is REJECTED, H-RECURRING-PAYMENT-FAILURES is SUPPORTED.
The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two critical/high unknowns (U-FAILURE-BACKLOG-CORRELATION, U-COMPETING-MECHANISMS) as VOBs rather than resolving them before release.

What was released: the IBAN-failure count deliverable from DA-PAY (work item W-WI-1, DONE), producing M-IBAN-FAILURE-COUNT = 5.0; release scope was limited to quantify_refund_failure_ticket_correlation:DA-PAY per the solution design.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds: the narrow, achievable DA-PAY deliverable shipped while the ticket-correlation (DA-TCK) work, the root-cause fix, and rate computation remain unfinished and are documented as limitations.
The chatbot solution requested by SH-SUP was not pursued, consistent with success criterion SC-NO-RESPONSE-SPEED-REMEDY, since its underlying hypothesis is rejected by E-01/E-02.
limitations_explained: Three verification obligations remain OPEN and outside release scope: VOB-U-FAILURE-BACKLOG-CORRELATION (what share of the backlog ties to IBAN failures vs other causes), VOB-U-COMPETING-MECHANISMS (whether delay, visibility gap, or capacity shortfall also contribute), and VOB-R-3 (total refund volume needed to turn the failure count into a rate).
The remedy that would address the root cause (SR-R-IBAN-VALIDATION-FIX: strengthen IBAN validation at refund submission) was marked not feasible in contest time and is left unfinished.
Only a raw count (5 IBAN failures) could be produced because total refund transaction volume (U-FAILURE-RATE-DENOMINATOR) is still OPEN, so no failure rate can be computed yet.

DA-TCK (tickets) completeness is UNKNOWN, so it is uncertain whether a refund-id linkage field exists to join tickets to refund failures (needed for M-FAILURE-TICKET-CORRELATION-R and SR-R-TICKET-REFUND-LINKAGE); this correlation metric currently has no value.

The released scope rests on two unverified assumptions: A-FAILURES-DRIVE-TICKETS (that these refund failures actually generate the repeat tickets, with no direct record joining a specific failure to a specific ticket) and A-SAMPLE-PERIOD-REPRESENTATIVE (that the 5 observed failures reflect an ongoing pattern, not a resolved historical anomaly).

Three conflicts (C-1, C-2, C-3) around the root-cause assertion remain OPEN in the record, reflecting that the stakeholder's response-speed framing (CL-01/CL-02/E-03) is still formally unresolved against E-02 even though it is treated as rejected for scoping purposes.
